title: The microbiome
examples: Are all the microbes in my gut good for me?
How do scientists study the microbiome?
Can eating certain foods change my gut bacteria?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the amazing world inside you. We are focusing on your gut microbiome.

draw.text: The Gut Microbiome: Tiny Life Inside

explain.say: Your gut contains trillions of tiny living things. These are the microbes that make up your microbiome.

draw.text: Trillions of Microbes in the Gut

explain.say: Many of these microbes are bacteria. They live there and interact with your body every day.
Some of these bacteria are helpful to your body. They help you digest the food you eat.
These helpful bacteria also help make important vitamins for you. For example, they help make Vitamin K.
In real life, eating fibre rich foods feeds these good bacteria. This helps keep your gut balanced and healthy.

faq.a: It is the community of bacteria and other microbes living in your digestive system. These microbes are essential for your health.

faq.q: Are all the microbes in my gut good?
faq.a: No, there are both helpful and harmful microbes. A healthy gut has a good balance of both types.
asks: Is it okay to have some bad bacteria?

faq.q: How do these bacteria help me digest food?
faq.a: They help break down complex carbohydrates that your body cannot digest on its own. This releases energy and nutrients.
asks: What is digestion help from bacteria?

faq.q: Can I get a gut imbalance?
faq.a: Yes, a gut imbalance means the bad bacteria are growing too much compared to the good ones. This is called dysbiosis.

faq.q: What foods help keep my gut healthy?
faq.a: Eating lots of fibre from fruits, vegetables, and whole grains is very important. These act as food for the good bacteria.
asks: What should I eat for my gut?

facts: The gut contains trillions of microbes, far exceeding the number of human cells.
Helpful bacteria assist in the digestion of complex carbohydrates.
These microbes synthesize essential vitamins, such as Vitamin K.
A balanced microbiome is key to overall digestive and immune health.

quiz.say: The primary role of gut bacteria is to:
quiz.why: The bacteria use the food you eat to create vitamins your body needs.

wrong.0: They help the immune system, but they do not fight off every single invading germ.
wrong.1: Fat digestion relies more on bile and enzymes, not solely the bacteria.
wrong.3: While gut health can affect mood, this is not their main, direct function.

quiz.say: If you eat a high-fibre diet, what happens to your gut bacteria?

options.show: They die off because of excess food.
options.say: They die off because of excess food.

options.show: They ignore the fibre and look for sugar.
options.say: They ignore the fibre and look for sugar.

options.show: They only eat the protein from the fibre.
options.say: They only eat the protein from the fibre.

options.show: They receive more food and thrive.
options.say: They receive more food and thrive.

quiz.why: Fibre is a type of carbohydrate that the good bacteria use as their main source of energy.

wrong.0: The bacteria need the fibre; it is their food source.
wrong.1: Fibre is specifically what they are adapted to break down.
wrong.2: Fibre is primarily carbohydrate material, not protein.

quiz.say: Which of these is a direct product of gut bacteria activity?
quiz.why: Bacteria are known to synthesize several vital vitamins needed by the human body.

wrong.0: Glucose is a simple sugar absorbed directly from digested starches.
wrong.1: Calcium is a mineral usually obtained from dairy or fortified foods.
wrong.3: Iron is a mineral that must be absorbed from food sources.
